text:
After closing, a mislaid note led our newest handler to ask questions about an earlier pet handoff and the status of a cabin-ready kennel. Routine desk work had already been completed for the evening, and the welcome team was moving through final checks for the next departures. The handler noticed the note near the counter and brought it to the senior coordinator before making any assumptions. The note referred to a traveler pairing and to a pet transfer that had already been cleared in the system, but it lacked the context needed for a proper handoff.

The senior coordinator reviewed the related records and confirmed that the animal file matched the boarding documents on hand. The team then checked the kennel label, the comfort supplies, and the boarding lane assignment to make sure nothing had been missed. Honey was not involved in this report, though the desk followed the same patient process used for every animal. No service issue had reached the passengers, and the brief confusion remained within the back office. The matter was handled as a record-keeping concern rather than an operational disruption.

To settle the matter, the note was removed from the active counter area and placed with the end-of-shift paperwork for review. The newest handler was told how to trace a note to the correct file, how to confirm whether it referred to an open task, and how to flag anything that seems out of sequence. The senior coordinator also reminded the team to keep separate any casual reminders from boarding documents so the desk stays clear and reliable. The companion animal service at Aurelia Skyways depends on calm checks, careful listening, and a shared habit of confirming details before action. Follow-up will include a short briefing at the next handover so the team can keep the same steady standard for future shifts.
